paper_title: Algorithms for Coloring Reconfiguration Under Recolorability Constraints
statement: Together with our sister paper [14], we have clarified several tractable/intractable cases of coloring reconfiguration under recolorability. Our analyses are summarized in Table 1, and give a better understanding of the complexity of coloring reconfiguration. However, the complexity status remains open for the case where a connected recolorability graph R is of maximum degree three and has at most one cycle.
context: One may expect that a shortest (f0 → fr )-reconfiguration sequence can be output also in linear time. However, Cereceda et al. [7] showed that there exists an infinite family of yes-instances for coloring reconfiguration with k = 3 whose shortest (f0 → fr )- reconfiguration sequence requires Ω(n2 ) length. Together with our sister paper [14], we have clarified several tractable/intractable cases of coloring reconfiguration under recolorability. Our analyses are summarized in Table 1, and give a better understanding of the complexity of coloring reconfiguration. However, the complexity status remains open for the case where a connected recolorability graph R is of maximum degree three and has at most one cycle.
